package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion Platform was compromised during its build process, resulting in official product updates being shipped with a sophisticated backdoor (SUNBURST). This allowed attackers to covertly gain unauthorized access to customer environments, exfiltrate sensitive data, and move laterally within networks. The malicious code was inserted upstream, making all distributed binaries during the affected period inherently untrustworthy and weaponizing the software supply chain.

execution_context.trigger: build-time (supply chain injection), runtime (on customer systems after Orion service starts)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks for specific system characteristics to avoid detection, introduces a randomized execution delay, then initiates an outbound network connection to a hardcoded command-and-control domain (avsvmcloud.com), exfiltrates system information, and awaits remote commands for execution, enabling persistent attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes covert outbound network communications to an attacker-controlled domain, exfiltrates detailed system information, and enables remote command execution, all while employing evasion techniques such as randomized delays and conditional execution to avoid detection by security tools.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate monitoring software should not initiate unsolicited outbound connections to unknown external domains, exfiltrate internal system data, or execute arbitrary remote commands. Such behaviors are inconsistent with standard update or telemetry mechanisms.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management or monitoring tools may contact vendor servers for updates or telemetry, but do so using transparent, documented endpoints and never execute arbitrary commands received from untrusted sources or employ covert evasion tactics.
key_indicators: Hardcoded C2 domain (avsvmcloud.com) in network communication logic
Randomized sleep/delay logic to evade automated analysis and sandboxes
Conditional execution based on system role and process name to avoid detection
Capability to receive and execute attacker-supplied commands remotely
Exfiltration of system information to external infrastructure

attack_chain.action: Attacker breaches SolarWinds build environment and injects malicious code into Orion Platform build process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is compiled and signed as part of official product updates.

attack_chain.action: Customers download and install contaminated Orion updates, deploying the malicious DLL.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is now present and active in customer environments.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code (SUNBURST) executes on customer systems, beacons to attacker-controlled domain, and awaits further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote access, can exfiltrate data, and move laterally within the network.

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com or other known SUNBURST C2 domains
Randomized execution delays in Orion service processes, inconsistent with normal update or telemetry behavior
Unusual process spawning or command execution initiated by SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll
Conditional execution logic that avoids running on domain controllers or in analysis environments
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (file hashes matching known malicious SUNBURST versions)
Presence of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with anomalous timestamps or digital signatures inconsistent with legitimate releases
network_indicators: Subsequent C2 domains as redirected by initial beacon (as documented in SUNBURST IOCs)
Unusual HTTP/S traffic patterns from Orion servers to external infrastructure not associated with SolarWinds
DNS queries to avsvmcloud.com and related domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for outbound connections and DNS queries from SolarWinds Orion servers to avsvmcloud.com and other known SUNBURST C2 domains. Validate the presence and cryptographic hashes of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll against threat intelligence for known malicious versions. Analyze Orion service logs for randomized execution delays, suspicious process activity, and evidence of remote command execution. Deploy EDR/XDR solutions to flag unexpected network or process behaviors originating from Orion-related binaries, and correlate with known SUNBURST indicators of compromise.
